_comment: Single source for claim_discipline.mjs in this repo and in nexus. test/ is not published; docs/ is. Do not copy this list into another file.

rules.why: a hash chain is tamper-evident, not immutable: the file can still be deleted or truncated
masking hides a value; a predicate over a protected column can still answer questions about it
rules.use: the values your policy protects are masked before they reach it

rules.why: absolute, and contradicted by the inference channel this project documents itself
rules.use: protected values masked before they leave

rules.why: only access through the gateway is logged — the reason conarium-reconcile exists at all
rules.use: every access through Conarium is logged

rules.why: releasing a policy-approved disclosure to an AI client is what the product does
rules.use: raw values stay in your perimeter — only policy-approved disclosure leaves

rules.why: one receipt naming an object clears further statements against it: that is object attribution
rules.use: attributable to receipt(s) for the same table

rules.why: the payload is a signed assertion by the issuer, not proof the transformation ran
rules.use: a signed assertion by the Issuer that the transformation was applied

rules.why: there is no SOC 2 audit; LIMITATIONS says so, and readiness is not ours to assert
rules.use: name what exists — no SOC 2 audit, no independent penetration test

rules.re: never (?:receive,? see,? or store|see) your data
rules.why: the website stores a waitlist email, forwards chat to a third-party model, and keeps host logs
rules.use: scope it in the sentence — the data Conarium governs never reaches us
